patterns.property: key letter position: slot A (choices as stored in items.json)
patterns.evidence: Key is the first listed choice in 64/72 items by these four authors (B 16/18, F 15/18, G 16/18, H 17/18) against 25% chance; batch-wide slot A holds 73/152. E.g. ITR2-G-P1A-1 key "arrange" listed first; ITR2-H-P3B-4 key "not shiny" first; ITR2-B-P3B-3 key "Less soreness, although the climb felt harder" first. Moot ONLY if choices are reshuffled before students see them; if this order is served it is the strongest tell in the batch.

All 22 author-E keys are the last listed choice (A 0, B 0, C 0, D 22). E.g. ITR2-E-P1A-1 key "Asking Lissa to join a birthday boat trip" is 4th; ITR2-E-P3A-5 "income" 4th. Same caveat: only a tell if this order is served.

patterns.property: key letter position: never slot A
patterns.evidence: Author A keys sit at B 9 / C 8 / D 5 / A 0 of 22; option A is never the key. Same caveat about serving order.

patterns.property: key names a change/arc/outcome (changed, turns into, grew, shaped/reshaped, proved its worth, saved, improved, stopped..began, taught, helped)
patterns.evidence: Where change/outcome wording varies across the four options, the key carries it in 12/14; in 7 of those the key is the ONLY option with it. Examples: ITR2-A-P3B-2 "a boy’s fear turns into interest"; ITR2-C-P3A-5 "how large shop windows changed the way people shopped"; ITR2-G-P3A-5 "whose own gifts then reshaped the collection"; ITR2-B-P2A-4 "How the writer’s view of jump rope changed". Exceptions: ITR2-C-P2A-3 (distractors "learned"/"helped", weak verbs), ITR2-F-P3A-6 (distractor "were improved"). A student learns: on main-idea, pick the option that tells a before/after story; it also tends to be the most upbeat.

patterns.property: key never has the highest word overlap with the passage
patterns.evidence: Share of option content words (stemmed) found in the passage: key is the top-overlap option in 0/22 inference items and the lowest in 11/22 (unstemmed metric: 1/22 top, 10/22 lowest). E.g. ITR2-C-P3A-1 key 0.67 vs two distractors at 1.00; ITR2-F-P3B-2 key 0.38 vs 0.88; ITR2-E-P3A-2 key 0.29 vs 0.86. Needs the passage to apply, but only as word-matching, not comprehension: "the option that echoes the text most is never the inference" removes one option every time. Partly the construct (an inference should not be verbatim), but it is perfectly consistent across all six inference-writing authors. Not seen in detail (14/43 top) or main-idea (5/20 top).

patterns.property: key carries a hedge (some, often, usually, can, might, few, many)
patterns.evidence: 78% on a small base, and weak: in 5 of the 7 another option is also hedged (ITR2-A-P3A-4 key "Some helmet designs..." vs distractor "Some woodpeckers ...only..."; ITR2-D-P3A-1 three options hedged). Key uniquely hedged only in ITR2-C-P2A-2 "He had often bought the same spices" and ITR2-G-P3B-5 shares with one. Two hedged distractors are never keys: ITR2-C-P3B-1 "Few people signed up...", ITR2-G-P3B-1 "mostly quiet". Batch-wide hedges are mixed (19/43).

patterns.property: key is the longest option in words (ties counted)
patterns.evidence: Non-vocabulary items by F: key ties for or holds the most words in 12/16 against 7.8 expected from ties at chance (49%). By characters it is uniquely longest only 4/18, so it is a mild word-count lean, not a stand-out key. E.g. ITR2-F-P2A-2 "to show that Mr. Nyberg had started learning new tablet skills on his own"; ITR2-F-P3B-4 "How a doubted signalling plan proved its worth to a mountain village". Author B is next at 11/15 (73%), just under the bar.

patterns.property: over-general / categorical distractor (generic class subject: birds, the human body, market sellers, young collectors, most kinds of fish, railways) is never the key
patterns.evidence: Judged by hand, so count is approximate. In 6 main-idea items one option widens to a generic class; it is never the key (0/6): "Birds that strike hard objects rely on shock-absorbing skulls" (A-P3A-1), "How the human body heals itself after different injuries" (B-P3B-2), "how market sellers keep track of the names of all their customers" (C-P2A-3), "how young collectors learn that a rock’s colour is worthless" (H-P3B-6), "why the males of most kinds of fish carry their young" (A-P2B-2), "Railways made life better for farming villages" (D-P3B-3). The textbook recipe, but used uniformly by 5 authors.

checked_clean: purpose: distractor recipe "to explain why..." - key carries "explain" 2/15 where it varies (13%); every one of 15 varying purpose items has an explain-distractor. Just above the 0% bar but the nearest miss in the batch: a student learns "explain" options are usually wrong.
key length rank by characters (batch): uniquely longest 30/152, uniquely shortest 33/152 - both near 25%; no kind exceeds 6/20 (main-idea shortest) or 13/44.
key longest by word count (batch, ties): 74/139 - mixed; per kind 7/14 to 13/21; per author non-vocab A 8/16, B 11/15, C 6/15, D 6/15, E 9/16, G 7/13, H 7/14 (F listed as pattern).
two-part "X and Y" options: batch 13/27; main-idea 8/16; detail 5/7 (71%, under bar); purpose 0/2.
hedges (some/often/may/can/few/many/about/several) batch: 19/43; main-idea 2/5; purpose 1/8; detail 3/8; not-except 2/3.
absolutes (all/only/never/every/full/any/at once) batch: 5/18 - mostly carried by distractors but key has it in 5 (e.g. ITR2-F-P3B-6 "without any dispute", ITR2-B-P2A-1 "the whole minute"); not 0%.
contrast / comparison words (but, although, rather, than, still) batch: 6/23; inference contrast 2/4.
negation (not, no, without, barely) batch: 6/10 - mixed.

first word / grammatical frame of key unique in its set (non-vocabulary): 39/75 vs ~52% expected; per author A 6/11, B 9/13, C 4/10, D 4/5, E 8/13, F 2/9, G 1/7, H 5/7 - none clears 75% on enough items except D 4/5 and H 5/7 which sit at their expected 4.3 and 4.5.
purpose leading verb: key verb (show/give/explain/tell/name/set up/sum up) unique in set 9/18 - mixed; "show" in key 7/14.
word overlap with the prompt: batch key highest 12/51, lowest 35/51; purpose key lowest 12/17 (71%, under bar) - purpose stems quote a phrase the distractors also reuse; a mild lean, not a tell.

word overlap with the passage: batch key top 39/134, bottom 42/134; detail top 14/43; main-idea top 5/20; purpose 7/22; not-except key lowest 8/13 (construct: the EXCEPT option is the one not in the passage).

centrality (key shares the most words with the other three options): batch 57/101; main-idea 14/20 (70%); author G 6/7 and not-except 5/6 are on 0-4 shared words with ties counted as max (unique max only in 1 not-except item) - noise.
vocabulary sets: all four options are senses of the target word in every item (30/30), no odd-one-out by part of speech; key uniquely shortest 5/30, uniquely longest 2/30.
tone: positive-outcome wording in keys is concentrated in main-idea (folded into the change/arc pattern); in purpose/detail/inference keys are not systematically the most positive or moderate option.
identical or near-identical key wording across items: no pair of keys reaches Jaccard 0.34 on content words; no reused key formula across passages.

minimal-pair distractors (key and one distractor differ in one element, e.g. ITR2-C-P3B-4 "for very little" / "for a high price", ITR2-B-P3B-3 2x2 grid, ITR2-H-P3B-5 roles reversed): key sits inside the pair in each case seen (3 of 3) but the pair also leaves 2 options, so it narrows to 50%; too few to call.
